newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog says time not right for power probe.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog says time not right for power probe.

text.p: British electricity industry watchdog Professor Stephen Littlechild said on Thursday he believed a monopoly investigation into electricity prices was not needed at the current time.
Littlechild, addressing an industry conference, was responding to commercial customers requests for a monopoly investigation into the pool, the wholesale market for electricity.
Im not convinced the time is right for a major investigation of that kind, he told the Utility Buyers Forum. Adding that this did not mean he was satisfied with the pools operation.
Major electricity consumers are concerned that the pool prices have been moving up since last year and are worried about the impact on electricity supply contracts for April this year.

Littlchild said he recognised that the pool was slow to consider reforming the way it operated, but he was uncertain an probe by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission would be the best solution at this stage.

He said the pool's move to offer customers two seats on its executive committee was a step in the right direction. But industry customers were not happy with this and said they would prefer to establish a customers' forum to hold a regular dialogue with the pool.
